walkthroughs.body_html:
Fertiliser washes into rivers.

Algae bloom and block sunlight. Plants die, decomposers multiply, using up oxygen. Fish suffocate. State the four steps in order.

Lichens indicate clean air; their absence signals SO₂. Mayfly larvae indicate clean water; bloodworms suggest pollution.

Indicator species are cheaper than chemical tests and show long-term conditions.

Methods: protected areas, captive breeding, seed banks, controlling invasive species, sustainable fishing quotas.

Gateway expects you to evaluate — cost vs ecological benefit and to whom.

mcqs.q: Why are food chains usually limited to about 4 or 5 trophic levels?
options: Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
Insulin works on muscles and glucagon works on the brain.
There aren't enough types of animals to fill more trophic levels.
Only ~10 percent of energy is transferred between trophic levels; eventually too little energy remains to support another level.
Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.
Humans evolved directly from chimpanzees, which is why chimps still exist as a less-evolved version.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
No — humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor; both have evolved from it.

mcqs.q: How do insulin and glucagon work together to regulate blood glucose?
options: They are antagonistic — insulin lowers blood glucose (cells take up glucose, store as glycogen); glucagon raises it (glycogen broken back down to glucose).
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
Insulin works on muscles and glucagon works on the brain.
Insulin and glucagon both lower blood glucose using different mechanisms.
